content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to read a protected [product_name] program without knowing the password?
Anything is possible—just request the password.
You can only access the program if you know the password.

If you don't know the password, you can only erase the password along with the program. The [product_name] will be usable again, but you'll need to reprogram it. See [url] for a guide on deleting both the program and the password.
In older versions of [product_name], it might have been possible to read or retrieve the password. You can try searching online for more information.
The general password for all [product_name] devices is ****.
Hi, that was a joke, wasn't it?
Yes, obviously that was a joke. All passwords use ****.
There are other passwords, for example *****. But generally, [product_name] devices use four stars.
Passwords can only contain letters (A-Z), which limits guessing options.
Since this is just a discussion, perhaps it's better to use other ways to communicate, like Meet&Talk. The forum may not need this thread.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members discuss whether it's possible to access a protected [product_name] program without the password. Most responses indicate the program cannot be read or retrieved without the correct password, and the only solution is to delete both the password and the program, which means reprogramming the device. Some mention older versions may have had vulnerabilities, but this is uncertain.
analysis.user_expectations: The original poster hopes to recover or read a protected program from [product_name] hardware without knowing the password and prefers to avoid erasing the existing program.
